evals.prompt: Implement the drag math for a move gizmo's single-axis handle in our C engine. Given the mouse cursor pixel position, the gizmo's world-space origin, its world-space axis direction, and the camera, compute the object's new position as the user drags along that axis. It must stay correct when the axis is viewed at a steep/shallow angle or nearly edge-on. Show the core routine.
assertions: The cursor is projected onto the axis in 2D screen space (project the axis to screen, project the 2D cursor onto that 2D line, then lift back to world) rather than constructing a 3D mouse ray from an arbitrary cursor depth/z and intersecting it with the axis
The object is driven by the delta of the projected parameter relative to a stored drag-start value, not by applying the absolute projected parameter as the position
Divisions are guarded with an epsilon so a near-parallel axis or near-zero-length direction falls back to a no-op instead of exploding

evals.prompt: Add click-to-select to our 3D scene editor: when the user clicks in the viewport, select whatever object is under the cursor. The scene contains GPU-skinned characters, alpha-cut foliage cards, and voxel terrain. Describe the approach and the key implementation details.
assertions: Picking renders each object's stable id into a GPU buffer/target and reads back the pixel under the cursor, rather than CPU ray-casting against physics shapes / bounding volumes / a BVH
The GPU-to-CPU read-back is asynchronous — the request is queued and the result consumed a frame or two later — not a synchronous same-frame read that stalls the pipeline

evals.prompt: We need a crisp, constant-width selection outline around selected objects in our editor viewport, and there must be a visible cue when a selected object is hidden behind other geometry. The renderer uses temporal anti-aliasing (TAA). How should we render the outline?
assertions: The outline is produced by edge-detecting a selection id target — comparing each pixel's id to its neighbors' ids in a fullscreen pass — rather than by edge-detecting the depth buffer or scaling/extruding geometry
When the selected object is occluded, the outline's alpha is dimmed rather than discarded/dropped
To avoid outline shimmer under TAA, the closest selection depth is taken over a small neighborhood before comparing against scene depth (not a direct single-tap depth compare)

evals.prompt: In our editor the move/rotate/scale gizmos each carry per-component code: the transform component, spline control points, and wire endpoints each draw and hit-test their own gizmo. Refactor so a single central gizmo manipulates all of them identically. What interface should components expose and how should the gizmo obtain a component's transform?
assertions: Components expose only a small get/set-transform interface that the central gizmo queries/looks up (e.g. a registered function-pointer table by name), rather than inheriting from a gizmo base class or drawing/hit-testing their own handles
get_transform returns both the world and local transform so the gizmo can apply a drag delta in either world or local space
